chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Zurarah, who said:

I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man entered with his son. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked, 'What is your son's trade?' He said, 'Tannakhus (buying slaves to resell).' He said to him, 'Do not buy a slave and then resell him. When you buy a head (slave), let its price not be seen in the scale of the balance. There is no head whose price is seen in the scale of the balance that does not succeed. When you buy a head, change its name, feed it something sweet when you possess it, and give charity on its behalf with four dirhams.'

key_terms.التَّنَخُّسُ: Speculative buying, specifically buying slaves to resell them for profit.
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ عَنْهُ: Give charity on behalf of (the slave).
key_terms.رَأْساً: A head, referring to an individual slave.
key_terms.كِفَّةُ الْمِيزَانِ: The scale of the balance, used here metaphorically for the price tag or visible cost.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying slaves for resale in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between speculative trading (*tannakhus*) and genuine acquisition by advising the buyer to conceal the price on the scale, symbolizing that the transaction is for utility rather than pure profit. He further emphasizes ethical treatment and spiritual care by recommending sweet food for the slave and offering four dirhams in charity (*sadaqah*) on their behalf, linking material ownership with spiritual success (*falah*).
